newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rebound, upside potential limited.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rebound, upside potential limited.

text.p: Polish shares rebounded in higher volume but analysts saw little short-term upside potential as the market still looked fairly valued despite its 6.6 percent fall late last week and on Monday.
Analysts said several small-cap stocks might record sharp swings this week following monthly reports for February earnings, most of which are due later on Tuesday.
"It seems...we are going to have a horizontal trend in the next few days, maybe longer," said Jan Koch, a trader at Polish Development Bank brokerage said.
Some analysts said a dip was possible in the next sessions.

Analysts said that despite some blue-chip gains on Tuesday many heavyweights including Elektrim, now trading at 24 times prospective 1997 earnings, had litte room for growth, with the whole market priced at 14 times 1997 earnings.
The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.7 percent, to 16,758, and turnover rose 25.5 percent to 180.5 million zlotys on three markets as 52 issues rose, 21 fell and 18 were flat.

Some analyst stressed the overall economic climate remained positive, helped by Monday's news that consumer prices rose only 1.1 percent in February, which could protect the bourse from falling below 16,500.
Espebepe tumbled 9.6 percent, extending Monday's plunge, after a decision on its possible debt write-off deal was postponed until April 14 on Friday, traders said.
They said Kable jumped 7.1 percent to 39.1 zlotys on good February earnings while Okocim, down 9.5 percent, could be hit by expectations of poor results due later on Tuesday.
The WIG index closed at 1,652.2 points in continuous trade, one percent down from the regular session, in 11.9 million zloty turnover.
